title: How LLMs Work: Tokens, Context Windows and Generation

scenes.subtitle: Tokens, next-token prediction, the context window, and the controls you have.

scenes.title: Your phone keyboard already does this
scenes.body: Type **"Happy birthday to"** and the keyboard suggests **"you"**. It guessed the most likely next word from patterns it has seen. An LLM does the same thing, at a much bigger scale, one token at a time.

items.text: An LLM is that idea, scaled up enormously
It predicts the next piece of text, again and again

scenes.title: Plausible text, not looked-up facts
scenes.body: The model writes what is **likely**, not what it has **checked**. It can be confidently wrong (a "hallucination"), and it knows nothing after its training cut-off. That's why agents get tools and documents.

scenes.heading: Tokens: the units a model reads and writes

cards.title: About 4 characters
cards.body: per token for English text. Code and other languages often use more.

cards.title: Count, don't guess
cards.body: The API has a free token-counting endpoint for the exact model you use.

scenes.title: Tokens are like a taxi meter
scenes.body: A taxi charges by the kilometre, both ways. The API charges by the token: **input** tokens you send, and **output** tokens it writes, and output costs more.

items.text: **Cost**: you pay per input token and per output token
items.sub: output tokens usually cost several times more

items.text: **Limits**: every request has a maximum size
items.sub: the context window, and a cap on the reply

items.text: **Speed**: replies are generated one token at a time
items.sub: longer answers take longer: streaming helps

scenes.title: The context window is your exam desk
scenes.body: In an exam you can only use what is **on your desk**: the question paper, your rough sheet, and the answer sheet. The model can only use what is **in the request**, and its answer must fit on the same desk.

scenes.heading: Everything must fit in the context window

steps.caption: Big windows still cost money: every token you send is billed

scenes.title: A doctor who never keeps your file
scenes.body: Imagine a doctor who forgets every patient the moment they leave. To get good advice, **you must bring your full file every visit**. The model is that doctor; your app carries the file.

scenes.heading: The model has no memory between requests

left.title: What it feels like
items: You chat, and it "remembers" your name
It seems to learn during the conversation

right.title: What really happens
items: Your app **sends the whole conversation** every time
The model's weights never change while you chat
Forget to send history, and it's gone

items.q: How does an LLM generate text?
items.a: It predicts the **next token** from everything so far, adds it, and repeats until it decides the answer is complete. It produces likely text; it does not look facts up.
items.trap: Saying it "searches the internet" or "retrieves answers from a database". On its own, it does neither.

items.q: Why does a chatbot "remember" earlier messages if the model has no memory?
items.a: Because the **application resends the conversation history** with every request. The API is stateless; the app owns the memory.
items.trap: Saying the model "learns" from the chat. Its weights don't change while you talk to it.

scenes.question: Your app sends a new request without the earlier messages. What happens?
options: It doesn't know: the model has no memory between requests
It looks it up in its training data
scenes.explain: Each request is independent. The model only sees what you send in that request, so the app must resend the history.
